title: Scenario-driven batching architect and safe application pipeline
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Build a scenario-driven batching recommendation engine that profiles workloads across traffic patterns, proposes continuous batching parameters, and applies config changes via a guarded pipeline with automated rollback. This ticket covers the architecting of heuristics, the telemetry footprint required for safe decisions, and the integration points for shadow/apply/canary and rollback orchestration. The output should be a runnable POC that can run nightly on sampled workloads and a hardened operator workflow for gradual apply to Dedicated/Hosted routes.
acceptance_criteria: Profiles ingest daily traffic traces and produces workload fingerprints with deterministic buckets
Generates batching parameter proposals (max_batch_size, microbatch_window_ms, coalesce_threshold) with expected cost/latency delta estimates
Shadow-apply flow exists where proposals run in a mirrored traffic path with metrics captured for 24h
Automated rollback triggers based on tail-latency regressions, error-rate upticks, or >5% cost increase
Operator UI shows proposal diff, safety checks, and one-click canary + ramp controls
Prototype validated on three representative customer workloads with documented results
proposed_solution: 1) Telemetry: extend workload sampler to persist per-route sequence length distribution, request arrival inter-arrival distribution, KV cache hit ratio, prefix reuse metric, and historical batching outcomes. 2) Fingerprinting: create deterministic signatures (hot-path, cold-path, episodic) using quantized histograms and time-of-day clustering. 3) Heuristics engine: rule-based initial proposer that suggests conservative parameter deltas with bounds (e.g., +20% max_batch_size or -10ms microbatch window). 4) Simulation: replay sampler traces through a fast cost/latency simulator calibrated from the runtime microbenchmarks. 5) Guarded apply: shadow-apply -> canary (1%) -> ramp (1->10->50%) with automatic rollback and audit log. 6) Safety net: include manual approval step for proposals with medium/high customer impact and automatic rollback if metrics cross thresholds within the canary window.
tradeoffs: Aggressive batching reduces cost but can increase tail latency; the proposer favors cost-savings only when tail-latency impact is within tolerance
Heuristic rules are fast to ship but will be complemented by ML-driven ranking later; shipping with clear extensibility hooks minimizes rework
Shadow-apply increases compute during evaluation but avoids customer-facing regressions; we accept short-term cost for safety
Stricter rollback thresholds reduce risk but also reduce realized cost gains; thresholds will be tuned per-customer SLA
rollout_plan: 1) Nightly profiler job samples 24h of traffic and emits fingerprints
2) Proposer generates up to 3 candidate configs sorted by expected cost delta and risk score
3) Simulation runs candidate configs through a calibrated simulator and attaches expected deltas
4) Shadow-apply: mirror live traffic for 24h and collect telemetry in isolation
5) Canary: apply to 1% of traffic for 30m with stricter monitoring and automatic rollback triggers
6) Ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% over configurable windows if no triggers fire
7) Full apply or rollback and post-mortem recorded in Confluence and incident dashboard
